Rashi on Zevachim 7a:17:1.hebrew: למימרא: דעשה בת מינה דחטאת היא.

Rashi on Zevachim 7a:17:2.hebrew: והאמר רבא כו' על מי שמחוייב עולה כשרה: אלמא לאו מיניה הוא, דהא עבירות עשה בידו שהפריש עולה עליהן.

Rashi on Zevachim 7b:10:1.hebrew: פסח מנלן - בין למצוה בין לעכב, דקס"ד לא אתי לן כשאר זבחים משלמים, דלא כתיב בההוא קרא דזאת התורה דאיתרבי כל הזבחים מיניה למצוה:
Rashi on Zevachim 7b:10:1.english: From where do we [derive this] for the Paschal offering - Whether as a [initial] requirement or as a [requirement that is] indispensable [after the fact]; for it would enter one's mind that it does not come to us like the other peace offerings, since it is not written in that verse, "This is the law" (Leviticus 7:37), from which all the offerings were included, as an [initial] requirement.

Rashi on Zevachim 7b:16:1.hebrew: מותר הפסח - שאבד, ונתכפר באחר, ונמצא הראשון:
Rashi on Zevachim 7b:16:1.english: A leftover Paschal offering - [An animal] that was lost, and [the owners] achieved atonement with another [animal], and the first was [then] found:

Rashi on Zevachim 7b:16:2.hebrew: לדבר הבא מן הצאן ומן הבקר - היינו שלמים, שהן באין מכל צאן ומכל בקר, בין זכרים בין נקבות; מה שאין כן בשאר זבחים, שהוקבעו או בזכר או בנקבה: עולה ואשם הוקבעו בזכרים; חטאת הוקבע בנקבות, והוקבע בזכרים, כגון שעיר נשיא, אינו בא בנקבה:
Rashi on Zevachim 7b:16:2.english: As an offering brought from the flock and from the herd - That is, a peace offering, which comes from any flock and any herd, whether males or females; unlike other sacrifices, which were fixed as either male or female: a burnt offering and a guilt offering were fixed as males; a sin offering was fixed as females, and [in some cases] was fixed as males, such as the goat of a prince, which does not come as a female.

Rashi on Zevachim 7b:17:1.hebrew: למצוה בשינוי קודש - בכולהו עשיות ילפינן מיניה, דהא כתיב ״ועשית״:
Rashi on Zevachim 7b:17:1.english: A mitzva [to sacrifice it] without deviation of [the type of] offering - We derive from it [the law] for all the [sacrificial] acts, for it is written, "and you shall perform [ve'asita]":

Rashi on Zevachim 7b:17:2.hebrew: הוא - משמע, פסח הוא בהוייתו, לשמו כשר, שלא לשמו פסול:
Rashi on Zevachim 7b:17:2.english: “It is” - This implies: it is a Paschal offering [only] in its [proper] state of being — [if offered] for its own name, it is valid; [if offered] not for its own name, it is invalid.

Rashi on Zevachim 7b:17:3.hebrew: דהכא והכא - בשינוי קודש ובשינוי בעלים, דהוא משמע אתרוייהו, כשהוא עשוי כמצותו משמע:
Rashi on Zevachim 7b:17:3.english: That [it is indispensable] both here and there - With regard to deviation of the offering's sanctity and deviation of the owner, for "it is" implies both of them; it implies [that the offering is valid] when it is done in accordance with its mitzva:

Rashi on Zevachim 7b:18:1.english: And we found [a source for] slaughter - [that it is disqualified] when done with a change of [designation as a different type of] sacrificial [offering] and with a change of owner.

Rashi on Zevachim 7b:1:1.hebrew: מקיבעא לא מכפרא - חטאת אינה מכפרת אעשה:
Rashi on Zevachim 7b:1:1.english: Not by its essence does it atone - A sin offering [does not atone] for [the violation of] a positive commandment.

Rashi on Zevachim 7b:1:2.hebrew: מקופיא מכפרא - הלכך על מי שמחוייב עולה כשרה, כיון [דהפריש] עולה, שייכי כולהו עשה שבידו אעולה, ותו לא שייך חטאת גביה. אבל מי שלא הפריש כלום, ועבירות עשה בידו, שייך חטאת גביה, דאילו הוה מתחייב חטאת, מכפר עשה מקופיא. הלכך חייל שמיה אחטאתו שנשחטה לשמו, לפוסלה:
Rashi on Zevachim 7b:1:2.english: It atones incidentally - Therefore, with regard to one who is obligated to bring an olah, [the sin offering slaughtered for its name] is valid: since he [already] set aside an olah, all the positive-commandment transgressions in his possession pertain to the olah, and a sin offering no longer pertains to him. But one who has not set aside anything, and has positive-commandment transgressions in his possession, a sin offering does pertain to him, for if he were obligated to bring a sin offering, it would atone for the positive commandment incidentally. Therefore, the name [of an olah] takes effect upon his sin offering that was slaughtered for its name, to disqualify it:

Rashi on Zevachim 7b:20:1.hebrew: ביום צוותו - סמוך לזאת התורה, ודרשינן סמוכין: ביום צוותו להקריב את קרבניהם — לרבות קרבנות שלא הוזכרו במקרא בענין שלמעלה:
Rashi on Zevachim 7b:20:1.english: In the day that He commanded - It is adjacent to "this is the law," and we expound adjacent verses: "In the day that He commanded… to present their offerings" — to include offerings that were not mentioned in the verse in the passage above.

Rashi on Zevachim 7b:21:1.hebrew: אף כל כו' - הלכך מצוה בפסח ילפינן משלמים דרבינן להו לעיל לשינוי קודש ולשינוי בעלים (ועשית פסח לעכב בכל עשיותיו בשינוי קדש, ואמרתם זבח פסח לעכב בזביחה בשינוי בעלים):
Rashi on Zevachim 7b:21:1.english: So too all [offerings], etc. - Therefore, we derive the [rule of] mitzva [only, not indispensability] regarding the Passover offering from peace offerings, which we included above for deviation from the offering and for deviation with regard to the owner. ("And you shall make the Passover offering" teaches that it is indispensable in all its acts of preparation, in the case of deviation from the offering; "And you shall say, It is the Passover sacrifice" teaches that it is indispensable with regard to slaughter, in the case of deviation with regard to the owner.)

Rashi on Zevachim 7b:22:1.hebrew: וכשלמים - כלומ' כיון דגלי קרא עכובא בזביחה, ילפינן שאר עבודות לעכובא מהיקשא דמצוה כשלמים, מה שלמים כו':
Rashi on Zevachim 7b:22:1.english: And like a peace offering - That is to say, since the verse revealed [that proper intent is] indispensable with regard to slaughter, we derive [that it is indispensable for] the other rites as well, from the juxtaposition [teaching] the mitzva [of intent], "like a peace offering: just as a peace offering..." etc.:

Rashi on Zevachim 7b:23:1.hebrew: הכי גרסי' אלא הוא למה לי לכדתניא [וכו'] אבל אשם לא נאמר כו' - ול"ג "כל מקום שנאמר בזביחה אינו אלא לעכב", דהך ברייתא לקמן היא בפירקין, בדינא ר' אליעזר ורבי יהושע, ול"ג ליה:
Rashi on Zevachim 7b:23:1.english: This is how we read it: "Rather, why do I need 'it is'? For it was taught [etc.]... but a guilt offering was not stated, etc." - And we do not read, "Wherever it is stated regarding slaughter, it is only to be indispensable," for that baraita appears later in this chapter, in the discussion of Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua, and we do not read it here.

Rashi on Zevachim 7b:24:1.hebrew: לכדתניא - כלומר, לגלויי על הוא דגבי אשם, דלא ילפינן פסול מיניה, כדמהדר ליה רבי יהושע לר' אליעזר לקמן בפירקין (זבחים דף י:), שהיה דורש: אשם הוא, לשמו כשר, שלא לשמו פסול. וקא מהדר ליה רבי יהושע: פסח נאמר בו הוא בשחיטה, לפיכך שלא לשמו פסול, אבל אשם כו':
Rashi on Zevachim 7b:24:1.english: As it is taught - That is to say, [this is] to reveal [the purpose of] the word "it is" ("hu") with regard to the guilt offering, [namely] that we do not derive invalidity from it, as Rabbi Yehoshua answers Rabbi Eliezer later in this chapter (Zevachim 10b), who would expound: "It is a guilt offering" — if [offered] for its own sake, it is valid; if not for its own sake, it is invalid. And Rabbi Yehoshua answers him: With the Paschal offering, "it is" is stated in connection with the slaughter; therefore, [offering it] not for its own sake is invalid. But the guilt offering, etc.

Rashi on Zevachim 7b:4:1.hebrew: לאחר מיתה - שמת בעליה, והקריבה היורש:
Rashi on Zevachim 7b:4:1.english: After death - The owner of [the offering] died, and the heir offered it.

Rashi on Zevachim 7b:4:2.hebrew: פסולה - לא עלתה, וצריך היורש להביא אחרת:
Rashi on Zevachim 7b:4:2.english: Unfit - It did not count [for the owner], and the heir must bring another [offering].

Rashi on Zevachim 7b:5:1.english: There is an owner - For the heir is its owner.

Rashi on Zevachim 7b:5:2.hebrew: דוקא קאמר מר - אי פליגי אדרבא, ובעי לאתויי אחריתי? או דלמא דאי איכא כמה עשה גביה, דיורש מכפרא, אם לא שינה בה. ומיהו היכא דשני, לא בעי לאיתויי אחריתי, דהא איהו לא נדר מידי:
Rashi on Zevachim 7b:5:2.english: Is the Master speaking specifically? - [Meaning:] Does he disagree with Rava, and [does the heir] need to bring another [offering]? Or perhaps [he means] that if there are several positive commandments [outstanding] against him, the heir's [offering] atones for them, if [the heir] did not change it [i.e., slaughter it for a different owner]. But nevertheless, where [the offering] was changed, he need not bring another, since he himself did not vow anything:

Rashi on Zevachim 7b:7:1.english: A burnt offering is a gift: It does not come to atone for a positive commandment directly, but rather, after repentance has atoned for the positive commandment, it comes for receiving favor, like a person who sinned against a king and appeased him through advocates, and when he comes to greet him, he brings a gift with him.

Rashi on Zevachim 7b:7:2.hebrew: היכי דמי - כלומר, היכי דמי שתהא באה לכפרה:
Rashi on Zevachim 7b:7:2.english: What are the circumstances - That is, what are the circumstances in which [the burnt offering] would come for atonement?

Rashi on Zevachim 7b:7:3.hebrew: אי דליכא תשובה - אעבירות עשה שבידו:
Rashi on Zevachim 7b:7:3.english: If there is no repentance - [This refers] to the transgressions of a positive commandment that he has in his hand.

Rashi on Zevachim 7b:7:4.hebrew: זבח רשעים תועבה - פסוק הוא במשלי (כא):
Rashi on Zevachim 7b:7:4.english: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination - It is a verse in Proverbs (21).

Rashi on Zevachim 7b:9:1.hebrew: למה באה לפני עולה - כל מקום שמביא חטאת ועולה, חטאת קודם, כדיליף לקמן בפרק כל התדיר (זבחים דף פט.):
Rashi on Zevachim 7b:9:1.english: Why is it brought before a burnt offering - Wherever one brings a sin offering and a burnt offering, the sin offering comes first, as [the Gemara] derives below in the chapter Kol HaTadir (Zevachim 89a):

Rashi on Zevachim 8a:1:1.english: “And the priest shall take” - This is an expression of collection.

Steinsaltz In-Depth comment #1 on Zevach.english: These matters raise a question that early and later commentators discussed in various ways: According to this, what is the meaning of the statements made above that a burnt offering atones for positive mitzvot? Ba'al ha-Turim in his commentary on the Torah (Leviticus 1:4) wrote that even though, as stated here, when one repents, he is forgiven, nevertheless, the atonement is not complete until he brings a burnt offering. The Ramban, however, wrote in his commentary on the Torah (Leviticus 1:4) that those liable for intentional violations of positive mitzvot, even though no punishment is decreed upon them in the Torah, nevertheless, they transgressed God's will and are not favored before Him, and the burnt offering brought as a gift — through it, he becomes favored before God and atoned. From Rashi's words here, it appears that even though it is said that a burnt offering atones for positive mitzvot — the intention is not for actual atonement (i.e., the actual forgiveness of the sin, cleansing the person from the sin), because this has already been fully accomplished through repentance, but rather it involves atonement in the sense that through it, the sinner appeases God when he wishes to see His face (and this is also one of the meanings of the term atonement, like "I will appease his face with a gift... and after that, I will see his face" (Genesis 32:21). See also in Iggeret HaTeshuva by the Baal HaTanya, Chapter 2).

Steinsaltz In-Depth comment #2 on Zevach.english: From the Greek <greek>δῶρον</greek> (doron), meaning gift or present. Some wrote that perhaps the primary atonement of the burnt offering is for positive commandments that one neglected unwittingly, and for which he did not repent (for this, the disqualification of "sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination" is not applicable) (Ḥazon Yeḥezkel).

Steinsaltz In-Depth comment #3 on Zevach.english: One who violated a positive mitzva (that is not punishable by karet) and repented — is forgiven immediately. (Rambam Sefer HaMadda, Hilkhot Teshuva 1:4).

Steinsaltz In-Depth comment #4 on Zevach.english: The origin of the word is in Greek <greek>δῶρον</greek> (doron) — a gift, an offering.

Steinsaltz on Zevachim 7a:17.english: And Rava says: A sin offering atones for those obligated in a positive mitzvah, due to a *kal vaḥomer*. What is the *kal vaḥomer*? If a sin offering atones for those who are liable for *karet* offenses, which are severe, all the more so should it not atone for those who are liable for positive mitzvot, which are less severe transgressions?

Steinsaltz on Zevachim 7b:2.english: And Rava says: A burnt offering that one slaughtered not for its sake is prohibited from having its blood sprinkled not for its sake.

Tosafot on Zevachim 7a:17:1.hebrew: על חייבי עשה לא כל שכן: מהאי קל וחומר הוה לן למימר דאפילו מקיבעא מכפרא, אלא דאינה מכפרא הואיל ועיקרא למילתא אחריתי קאתיא, ואהני קל וחומר לקופיא.
Tosafot on Zevachim 7a:17:1.english: All the more so for those liable for a positive mitzvah: From this *kal vaḥomer*, we should have said that a sin offering atones even by its essence. However, it does not atone by its essence because it was primarily designated for another matter. This *kal vaḥomer* is only effective for incidental atonement.

Tosafot on Zevachim 7b:13:1.hebrew: ואמרתם זבח פסח - האי קרא כתיב ברישא דפרשה: "ושמור את חודש האביב". הוה ליה לאוקומי [בשינוי בעלים] באם אינו ענין. אלא משום דכייל בה כל עבודות, דכתיב "ועשית פסח" — [דמשמע] מסתמא כל עשיות — הלכך מוקי ליה לשינוי קודש:
Tosafot on Zevachim 7b:13:1.english: "And you shall say: It is the Passover sacrifice" - This verse is written at the beginning of the passage: "Observe the month of Aviv" (Deuteronomy 16:1). [Therefore] it should have been established [as referring to deviation of the owner] by [the principle of] "if it is not needed for its [original] matter." But because it includes in it all the services, as it is written, "and you shall make a Passover" — [which] implies, without qualification, all acts of making — therefore [the Gemara] establishes it as [referring to] deviation of the sanctity (the type of offering):

Tosafot on Zevachim 7b:15:1.hebrew: וזבחת פסח - בסוף התודה (מנחות פב.) דריש לה במשנה לדבר שבחובה [שהיא באה מן החולין], והתם בגמרא נמי מייתי דרשא דהכא:
Tosafot on Zevachim 7b:15:1.english: "And you shall sacrifice the Paschal offering" - At the end of [the chapter] Todah (Menachot 82a), [the Mishnah] expounds it for a matter that is obligatory [that comes from unconsecrated animals]; and there, in the Gemara too, it cites the exposition found here:

Tosafot on Zevachim 7b:16:1.hebrew: ומאי ניהו שלמים - דעולה ליכא למימר, דאינה באה מכל צאן ובקר כדפי' בקונטרס דאינה באה נקבה. ועוד, איכא לקמן תלתא קראי, וההוא דאם כבש מוכח בהדיא דהוי שלמים. ועוד, דדוחין קדשים קלים אצל קדשים קלים ולא אצל קדשי קדשים, כדלקמן (זבחים דף ט.):
Tosafot on Zevachim 7b:16:1.english: "And what is it? A peace offering" - It cannot be said [that it is] an burnt offering, for it does not come from every [kind of] flock and herd, as [Rashi] explained in the commentary, since [a burnt offering] does not come [from] a female. Furthermore, below there are three verses, and the one [stating] "if it is a lamb" proves explicitly that it is a peace offering. Furthermore, [the rule is that] one may displace lesser sacred offerings to [be sacrificed alongside] lesser sacred offerings, but not to most sacred offerings, as [stated] below (Zevachim 9a):

Tosafot on Zevachim 7b:17:1.hebrew: וזבחת פסח לכדרב נחמן - בסיפרי פרשת עשר תעשר דריש כולהו בשנוי קודש, והכי איתא התם: "וזבחת" - אין לי אלא זביחה, שאר עבודות מנין? ואשינוי [קודש] קאי. ת"ל "ועשית". יכול אף הקטר חלבו? ת"ל "וזבחת". ואין זה בסוגיא שלנו:
Tosafot on Zevachim 7b:17:1.english: "And you shall sacrifice the Paschal offering," [which teaches] the statement of Rav Nachman - In the Sifrei, in the section of Aser Te'aser, [the Sifrei] expounds all of them as referring to a change of sanctity (shinui kodesh), and this is what it says there: "'And you shall sacrifice' — I have only slaughtering; from where do I know [the same for] other services? But [the verse] is speaking of a change of [kodesh] sanctity. [Therefore] the verse says, 'and you shall perform.' One might think that even burning its fat [is included]; [therefore] the verse says, 'and you shall sacrifice.'" But this is not [the line of reasoning] in our passage.

Tosafot on Zevachim 7b:17:2.hebrew: הוא לעכב בין הכא בין הכא - בשינוי קודש בכל עבודות, בשינוי בעלים בזביחה. אע"ג דהוא בזביחה כתיב בפרשת בא אל פרעה, וקרא דועשית בפרשת ראה אנכי — מכל מקום משמע "הוא" בהוייתו, כשהוא עשוי כמצותו, כדפי' בקונטרס. והשתא הא דקאמר "אשכחן זביחה, שאר עבודות מנא לן" — אשינוי בעלים קאי. עוד יש לפרש דבין בשינוי קודש בין בשינוי בעלים קבעי: מנא לן לעכב דהוא קאי דוקא אזביחה? ומדאפקיה רחמנא לשינוי בעלים בלשון שינוי קודש, אית לן לאוקומי הא דזביחה לעכב בין בשינוי בעלים בין בשינוי קודש. ושינוייא דהואיל וגלי גלי — לא ניחא להאי פירושא כמו לפירוש קמא:
Tosafot on Zevachim 7b:17:2.english: "It is" — to be indispensable, both here and there - With regard to deviation of the offering's sanctity, [it is indispensable] in all the Temple services; with regard to deviation of the owners, [it is indispensable] in the slaughter. Even though "it is" is written with regard to slaughter — in the section of "Come to Pharaoh" (Exodus 12), and the verse "and you shall perform" is in the section of "Re'eh" (Deuteronomy 16) — nevertheless "it is" implies [the offering] in its essential state, when it is done as commanded, as explained in the Kuntres [Rashi's commentary]. And now, when [the Gemara] says, "We have found [this for] slaughter; from where do we derive the other services?" — it refers to deviation of the owners. There is another way to explain: [the Gemara] was asking about both deviation of sanctity and deviation of owners: From where do we derive that it is indispensable, since "it is" refers specifically to slaughter? And since the Merciful One expressed [the law of] deviation of the owners in the language of deviation of sanctity, we must establish this [law] of slaughter as indispensable with regard to both deviation of the owners and deviation of sanctity. And the answer, "since it was revealed, it was revealed," is not as comfortable according to this explanation as according to the first explanation:

Tosafot on Zevachim 7b:21:1.hebrew: מה שלמים בין בזביחה בין בשאר עבודות לא חלקת בהן - וא"ת: כיון דכתיב "ועשית" פסח לעכב בשינוי קודש בכל עשיות, לשתוק קרא מזביחה ותיתי משלמים! דמה שלמים לא חלקת בין בשינוי קודש לשינוי בעלים למצוה, אף לפסח לא תחלוק לעכב:
Tosafot on Zevachim 7b:21:1.english: Just as a peace offering — whether with slaughter or with the other services — you did not distinguish between them - And if you ask: Since it is written "and you shall make" the Passover offering, to be indispensable in the case of deviation from the offering, in all the acts of making, let the verse be silent about slaughter, and it would be derived from peace offerings! For just as with a peace offering you did not distinguish between deviation from the offering and deviation with regard to the owner, [and it applies] as a mitzva only, so too with the Passover offering you should not distinguish, [so as] to make it indispensable:

Tosafot on Zevachim 7b:23:1.hebrew: אלא הוא למה לי - לקמן בפרק בית שמאי (זבחים דף לז:) ובפסחים פרק מי שהיה טמא (פסחים דף צז.) דריש "הוא" דפסח למעוטי תמורת פסח, ותרי "הוא" כתיבי. ובפסחים בסוף תמיד נשחט (פסחים דף סב:) דריש רבי אליעזר מ"הוא" דפסח: לא הוא כשר לשם אחרים, ולא אחרים כשרין לשמו. ורבי אליעזר לטעמיה, דאית ליה עכובא באשם, ולא מוקי ליה למימר: אבל אשם לא נאמר בו "הוא" כו':
Tosafot on Zevachim 7b:23:1.english: Rather, why do I need "it is" - Later, in the chapter Beit Shammai (Zevachim 37b), and in Pesachim, in the chapter Mi She'haya Tamei (Pesachim 97a), [the Gemara] expounds the "it is" of the Paschal offering as excluding a substitute for a Paschal offering, and "it is" is written twice. And in Pesachim, at the end of [the chapter] Tamid Nishchat (Pesachim 62b), Rabbi Eliezer expounds from the "it is" of the Paschal offering: It is not valid when [slaughtered] for the sake of others, and others are not valid when [slaughtered] for its sake. And Rabbi Eliezer follows his own reasoning, for he holds that [proper intent] is indispensable in the case of the guilt offering, and he does not establish [the verse] as saying: But with respect to a guilt offering, "it is" was not stated about it, etc.:

Tosafot on Zevachim 7b:24:1.hebrew: כל מקום שנאמר הוא בזביחה - פירש בקונטרס: ולא גרסינן ליה, משום דליתיה בברייתא דלקמן. ואין למחוק בשביל כך הספרים, דאפשר שהיא בברייתא בשום מקום בתוספתא:
Tosafot on Zevachim 7b:24:1.english: Wherever "it is" is stated, it refers to the slaughter - [Rashi] explained in the Kuntres: that we do not have this in our text, because it is not in the baraita that appears below. But one should not erase this from the books on that account, for it is possible that it is in a baraita somewhere, in the Tosefta.

Tosafot on Zevachim 7b:7:1.hebrew: עולה דורון היא - אע"ג דאעשה מכפרת, יותר מחטאת, דהא מכפרא מקיבעא:
Tosafot on Zevachim 7b:7:1.english: A burnt offering is a gift - Even though it atones for a positive commandment, more than a sin offering, for it atones from [what is] fixed:

Tosafot on Zevachim 7b:9:1.hebrew: ריצה פרקליט - אע"ג דאיכא עולת יולדת ומצורע ונזיר, דלא מייתי קרבן אלא לאישתרויי בקדשים, כדאמר בפרק בתרא דכריתות (דף כו.), ואפילו הם חטאתם קודמת לעולה, דלא חלקה תורה:
Tosafot on Zevachim 7b:9:1.english: "The advocate has appeased" - Even though there are the burnt offering of a woman after childbirth, a leper, and a nazirite, who bring their offering only in order to be permitted to partake of sacred things, as stated in the last chapter of Keritot (26a) — even [in] those [cases], their sin offering precedes the burnt offering, as the Torah did not make a distinction:

Zevachim 7a:17.english: And Rava says that a sin offering atones for those obligated to bring a burnt offering for violating a positive mitzvah, due to a *kal vaḥomer*: If a sin offering atones for those who are liable for transgressions for which one receives *karet* if one performs them intentionally, all the more so is it not clear that a sin offering atones for those liable for failing to fulfill a positive mitzvah?

Zevachim 7b:10:1.hebrew: פסח מנלן - בין למצוה ובין לעכב? דקא סלקא דעתך, לא אתי לן כשאר זבחים משלמים, דלא כתיב בההוא קרא ד"זאת התורה" דאיתרבי כל הזבחים מיניה למצוה:
Zevachim 7b:10:1.english: From where do we know about the Pesach offering? Both for the mitzvah (initially) and for it to be indispensable (disqualifying if not done correctly)? For it might have entered your mind that it does not come to us from the peace offerings like other animal offerings, because it is not written in that verse of "This is the law" from which all other animal offerings were included as a mitzvah:

Zevachim 7b:10:2.hebrew: ואם מן הצאן קרבנו כו' - לאו קרא יתירא קא דריש; אלא משמעותא דקרא משמע ליה הכי: ואם דבר הבא מן הצאן, דהיינו פסח שאינו בא אלא מן הצאן, היה קרבנו הרי הוא לזבח שלמים. ועל כרחך שלא בזמנו קאמר, דאי בזמנו הא ילפינן ליה לעיל דפסול:
Zevachim 7b:10:2.english: And if his offering is of the flock, etc. - He does not derive it from a superfluous verse; rather, the plain meaning of the verse implies this to him: And if a thing that comes from the flock, meaning a Pesach offering which comes only from the flock, was his offering, behold it shall be a peace offering. And you are forced to say that he is speaking about when it is not in its [appointed] time, for if it were in its [appointed] time, we already derived above that it is unfit:

Zevachim 7b:4.english: And Rava says: With regard to a burnt offering that is brought by its owner’s heirs after his death, if one slaughtered it with `shinnuy kodash`, i.e., for the sake of another type of offering, it is unfit, i.e., it does not satisfy the owner’s obligation, and the heirs must therefore bring another offering. But if it was slaughtered with `shinnuy be'alim`, i.e., for the sake of another person, it is fit, as the offering has no legal owner after the owner’s death.
